localityScope: Subic Bay project-area waters as named in the EIS; the EIS text reviewed here does not establish a single municipal boundary or exact fish station geometry.
question: What fish and aquatic-waterbody evidence does the Subic International Golf Club EIS report, and can its 2020 survey caption support current or site-specific species assertions?

primaryReport.citation: Subic Smart Community Corporation. Environmental Impact Statement: Subic International Golf Club Project. DENR-EMB EIA document repository (official PDF path under 2021/05; report issue date not independently verified).

pageLocators: Printed page 257, section 4.2.5 Fishes and Other Aquatic Fauna and methods
Printed pages 257-259, Table 4-48 and adjacent source footnote

studyContext.methodAsReported: The fish section says field observations and informal interviews with Subic International Golf Club personnel, particularly field guides and people encountered during the survey, were used for current aquatic-life information. It separately says fish composition data/information was also taken from the SBFZ PEPRMP study (identified elsewhere in the report as a 2012 study). The report does not identify the evidence mode for each Table 4-48 tick.
studyContext.tickFootnoteAsIndexed: A checkmark means fish species caught during exploratory fish surveys conducted during the dry and wet seasons in Subic Bay (PEPRMP, SBFZ; March-April and September 2012).
studyContext.lineageInterpretation: The 2020 caption, mixed observation/interview method, explicit 2012 composition source, and 2012 checkmark footnote do not support treating every table row as a 2020 specimen observation. Exact per-row source lineage is unresolved.

habitatContextAsReported.limitation: These are report labels and context only; the waterbody names are not normalized to authoritative geometry or a source-verified administrative crosswalk.

summaryCountReconciliation.reportSummaryAsIndexed: The narrative says Malawaan-Binictican River System and Olongapo Bay each have seven fish species, and Malawaan River has five.
summaryCountReconciliation.note: Counting indexed Table 4-48 checkmarks including Sarotherodon melanotheron yields one more than each narrative total; excluding that ubiquitous row yields 7/7/5. The report does not explain whether the invasive black-chin tilapia was excluded from the summary count. This is a text-derived reconciliation, not a visually verified recount.

tableFindings.transcriptionLimit: The full 22-row species-by-waterbody matrix was not copied into the public research repository. Counts and the three freshwater narrative labels above are retained as concise internal source findings; the indexed table text still needs page-image verification before any row-level reuse.

decision: Retain the report as a historical, mixed-source candidate lead spanning freshwater, brackish/estuarine, and coastal waters. Do not convert the 22 table rows or the three freshwater names into occurrence records, a current checklist, a fish-to-station mapping, or an app projection. Preserve verbatim source spellings until a taxonomic authority and the underlying evidence are reviewed.

rightsAndDisposition.itemSpecificReuseLicense: No item-specific license or permission to redistribute the EIS table, maps, or photographs was verified.
rightsAndDisposition.contentHandling: No PDF, page image, fish table, map, or EIS photograph was downloaded or retained. Only concise source facts and a limited set of verbatim name strings are recorded for internal research.

nextActions: Seek a lawful, directly accessible copy or page images of printed pages 257-259 and confirm the Table 4-48 cells, labels, footnote, and publication date visually.

Locate the cited 2012 SBFZ PEPRMP or underlying exploratory fish-survey tables; establish which rows derive from catches, interviews, literature, or the 2020 field work and reconcile the 7/7/5 summary counts.

Keep the freshwater fish spellings verbatim until a taxonomic crosswalk can be checked against the source and voucher/specimen evidence; do not infer present-day occupancy, native status, abundance, catchability, diet, or fishing permission.
Review item-specific reuse terms before copying species-by-waterbody rows, maps, or photographs into Bangwit or distributing them in an app or public data file.
